entities.summary: Pedro de Alcántara Álvarez de Toledo y Salm-Salm, 13th Duke of the Infantado, was a Spanish Army officer and politician who played a pivotal role in the early modern period of Spanish history. Born on July 20, 1768, in Madrid, Spain, he rose through the ranks of the Spanish military, earning recognition for his bravery and strategic prowess. Pedro de Alcántara served as a military officer during the Napoleonic Wars and later entered politics, becoming a key figure in the Spanish Cortes. His leadership and political acumen helped shape the country's government and politics during a time of great change and upheaval. Pedro de Alcántara's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as his actions and decisions had a lasting impact on the development of modern Spain. He died on November 27, 1841, leaving behind a legacy of service, duty, and patriotism.
